clue.text: Pile fruit up in five lines

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means placed above, so the fruit comes before the pile

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit
a rick is a stack of hay or straw

explanation.surface: Fruit heaped high, described in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' means the fruit sits on top, coming first in the answer; 'in' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A limerick is a humorous poem of five lines, rhyming AABBA.

clue.text: Somewhere to revel after dark — one tiro takes another in…

parts.note: after dark is night-time

indicators.note: takes ... in means one piece holds the other inside it
completes 'takes ... in', putting the learner inside the novice

parts.note: a cub is a beginner, as in a cub reporter
another tiro: L is the learner on a British L-plate

explanation.surface: A party spot open late, where one novice shows another round.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs into 3 down with dots. L stands for learner, from the L-plate British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: A club open late is a venue for dancing and partying.

clue.text: …pub where tiros can be seen outside, round about

indicators.note: the learners stand on the outside, enclosing the other letters

parts.note: two tiros are two learners, LL
O is round in shape
CA (circa) means about, of dates

explanation.surface: A bar where beginners gather outside, standing round.
explanation.walkthrough: Continues from 2 down. L is learner (from the L-plate), so two tiros are LL; CA is circa, Latin for about.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is Britain's word for one's nearest or regular pub.

clue.text: State cleared out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, signalling the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A country emptied of people.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something is to announce or assert it.

clue.text: With a few coins, chap becomes drunk

parts.note: the sou was an old French coin of small value, so several of them are sous
Ed is a man's name, a stock crossword stand-in for any chap

explanation.surface: A man with a handful of loose change goes off and gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds SOUSED, a common word for drunk; the grid as filed has BOUSED, and the first letter is unchecked, so a misread S is the likely slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Soused is informal for intoxicated, as if pickled in alcohol.

clue.text: It's worthless, raising nothing as an instalment

indicators.note: in a down entry raising lifts the letter higher up the column

parts.note: no-account means worthless, of no value
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Something valueless pays nothing when paid in part.
explanation.walkthrough: NO-ACCOUNT means worthless; 'raising' lifts its O (nothing) above the N in this down entry. 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying on account means paying part of a sum in advance of the whole bill.

clue.text: Animals when climbing shed a little

indicators.note: to shed something is to lose it, so the letter is dropped
in a down entry, climbing means reading upwards, so the word is turned round

parts.note: llamas are South American animals

explanation.surface: Animals scaling a slope lose a bit of fleece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when climbing' turns LLAMAS into SAMALL; 'shed' removes the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Small and little both mean of slight size.

clue.text: Woman on the way up after becoming a companion

indicators.note: the woman's name comes after the other piece in the answer

parts.note: becoming means fitting or proper, as is due

indicators.note: in a down entry, on the way up means written upwards, turned round

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman climbing up after gaining a new role as an escort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' turns ANN into NNA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman acting as chaperone to a young lady, in Spain especially.

clue.text: Frank's address

definitions.meaning: to address remarks to someone is to aim them at that person

explanation.surface: A man named Frank's home location.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain-spoken speech is direct, and to direct a letter or remark is to send it to someone.

clue.text: . Wonderful coat worn by soldier

indicators.note: the coat is worn, so the soldier's letters sit inside the coat's

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier wears an amazing coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic as an adjective is informal praise meaning marvellous or excellent.

clue.text: Acquainted with leading feature in pottery

parts.note: the chin juts out first on a face, so it is the leading feature
acquainted with something is aware of it

explanation.surface: Someone recognises a prominent feature on a piece of ceramic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is only a link here; 'leading feature' is a playful description of the chin, the part of the face that leads.
explanation.definitionFit: China is fine porcelain, and the wares made of it are pottery.

clue.text: Revenge of a literate sort

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange, so the letters of these two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A form of vengeance favoured by well-read people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' looks like a noun meaning kind, but it is the anagram signal on 'a literate'.
explanation.definitionFit: To revenge oneself is to hit back at someone who has done harm, i.e. strike back in kind.

clue.text: Stop a foreigner's money

definitions.meaning: a punctuation mark that halts a sentence, a two-dot pause
the currency unit of Costa Rica, and formerly El Salvador

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt payment of an overseas visitor's cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-dot punctuation mark is a stop in writing, and the colón is a Central American currency.

clue.text: Travel about in town and city

indicators.note: the turned-round word goes inside the town's name

parts.note: Colne is a market town in Lancashire, England

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for travel is written backwards

parts.note: to travel is to go

explanation.surface: Someone moves around in urban places.
explanation.walkthrough: Colne is a small Lancashire mill town; 'about' turns the word for travel round, and 'in' places it inside the town's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne (Köln) is a major German city on the Rhine.

clue.text: The place to hide lumber and wounded hero? Golly!

indicators.note: wounded means damaged, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A storeroom, and an injured hero exclaiming in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lumber' is British for clutter and junk, not timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A glory hole is a cupboard or room for stowing junk out of sight.

clue.text: Shown in good condition, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is spoken and another word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: taut can mean tidy and in good order, like a taut ship

explanation.surface: Something displayed in fine shape, or so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Shown in the sense of instructed: if you have been shown how, you have been instructed.

clue.text: Airborne manoeuvres are great fun

parts.note: anything airborne is high up
jinks are sudden dodging movements

explanation.surface: Aerobatics are a thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: High jinks means boisterous merrymaking and fun.

clue.text: Brave and noble, as seen in part of escutcheon

indicators.note: the noble is seen inside the heraldic band, its letters placed within

parts.note: a fess is a broad horizontal band across a heraldic shield
an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A courageous aristocrat shown on a coat of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: An escutcheon is a heraldic shield; the fess is its horizontal band.
explanation.definitionFit: Courageous people are without fear.

clue.text: Jack's to be seen vaguely blowing

parts.note: Jack is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is a sailor
to loom is to appear indistinctly, often large and threatening

explanation.surface: A sailor is dimly visible, perhaps through a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing' suggests wind, but it is the old sense of a flower blowing, opening into bloom. The 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower that blows is opening its petals, i.e. in bloom.

clue.text: Frenchwoman gets man in a state

indicators.note: the man is placed inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for Maine, a US state
Adam was the first man

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman finds her husband in a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a state' suggests agitation, but it is ME, Maine.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French courtesy title for a married lady.

clue.text: Fag's wearisome duty

definitions.meaning: in British use a fag is tiring drudgery, and it also means weariness
a soldier's ... are menial non-combat chores such as cleaning

explanation.surface: A public-school junior boy's tiresome chores.
explanation.walkthrough: A fag at a British public school was a junior boy doing chores for a senior, which colours the surface; here the word means tiredness.
explanation.definitionFit: Weariness and exhaustion are what 'fag' means in British slang, and soldiers' menial chores are fatigues.

clue.text: Complaint — only half of Pope's letter shows good command of language

parts.note: flu is an illness, a complaint

indicators.note: half of means only the first half of the letters are used

parts.note: an encyclic, or encyclical, is a letter from the Pope to bishops

explanation.surface: Only half the Pope's letter, sent despite illness, is fluently written.
explanation.walkthrough: ENCYCLIC is a variant of encyclical; its first half is ENCY.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluency is the ability to speak or write smoothly and easily.

clue.text: Top team gets ahead first

indicators.note: first puts the word for ahead before the team in the answer

parts.note: a team that is up is ahead in a game
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: The leading team gets in front early.
explanation.definitionFit: The upside of something is its top or upper face.

clue.text: Leave before the end of January — it's cold

parts.note: to park a car is to leave it standing somewhere

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, taken here from the month

explanation.surface: A suggestion to go away before January is out, because the weather is chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: PARKY is British slang for chilly weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Parky is informal British English for chilly, said of the weather.

clue.text: Some apparel I consider a survival from the past

indicators.note: some of these words means just part of them, a run of letters inside

explanation.surface: Some clothing strikes the speaker as a holdover from history.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object or custom surviving from an earlier era.

clue.text: Instrument with significance for a band leader

parts.note: a drum is a musical instrument
something of significance is major, important

explanation.surface: A musical instrument that carries special weight for whoever leads a band.
explanation.walkthrough: A drum major leads a marching band, twirling the mace.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum major marches at the front of a military or marching band, directing it.

clue.text: City gent without a single pound

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the man's letters surround the others

parts.note: a gent is a man
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A city gentleman who is completely broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean lacking, but it is the old sense 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan is a major city in northern Italy.

clue.text: Douglas here is left to face wild foeman

indicators.note: wild means uncontrolled, so the letters of the enemy word are scrambled

explanation.surface: A man named Douglas is abandoned to confront a savage enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas looks like a person but is the capital of the Isle of Man; 'wild' rearranges FOEMAN as EOFMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The town of Douglas is the capital of this Crown dependency in the Irish Sea.

clue.text: Weapon Knight doesn't use a lot

indicators.note: not using some letters means leaving them out of the knight's name

parts.note: Sir Lancelot was a knight of King Arthur's Round Table
a lot is a lot, taken as the three letters

explanation.surface: A knight hardly ever uses his weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knight' seems to be the subject, but it is Sir LANCELOT of Arthurian legend; dropping 'a lot' leaves the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear carried by a mounted knight in jousting.

clue.text: Book abridged in Greater Manchester

indicators.note: an abridged text is shortened, so the end of the book name is cut off

parts.note: Ecclesiastes is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A shortened volume read in north-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: ECCLES is a town in Greater Manchester, the metropolitan county round the city of Manchester; it is also the usual short form of the Bible book.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccles is a town lying within the Greater Manchester county area.

clue.text: Spy on his disturbed sleep

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An agent keeps watch on a man whose rest is troubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypnosis is a trance-like state resembling slumber, its name from the Greek for that state.
